quickQuestions.a: piBrick is an open-source handheld computer platform built around the Raspberry Pi Compute Module family, designed for makers who want a small Linux computer they can understand, modify and rebuild.

quickQuestions.q: Is the Raspberry Pi CM5 included?
quickQuestions.a: No. The piBrick PocketCM5 is a carrier-board and handheld platform. Raspberry Pi CM5, battery and NVMe SSD are sourced separately unless a specific bundle says otherwise.
A 5000 mAh LiPo is recommended. The mainboard uses a JST 2-pin 2.0 mm battery connector. Always verify polarity and battery protection before connecting it.
The PocketCM5 mainboard supports M.2 NVMe 2230 and 2242 drives. The piBrick package includes the small M2 fastening screw used to secure the SSD.

quickQuestions.q: Can I use piBrick PocketCM5 as a phone?
quickQuestions.a: No. piBrick PocketCM5 is designed and marketed as an open-source handheld computer, not as a smartphone or phone replacement. Its purpose is to provide a compact Linux computer with a physical keyboard for development, terminal access, remote administration, maker projects, and general computing on the go. Although people often ask about cellular support, that has never been the main goal of the project. Please think of piBrick as a pocket-sized Linux handheld computer rather than a phone.
Yes. The hardware design is published as open hardware. You can manufacture the PCB and source the remaining mechanical and electronic parts yourself.
The piBrick Discord community is the best place for build questions, troubleshooting, firmware discussion and project updates.
